newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN TOBACCO INDUSTRY GETS OFF LIGHTLY -STUDY.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN TOBACCO INDUSTRY GETS OFF LIGHTLY -STUDY.

text.p: South Africa's cigarette industry has seen its profit margin widen over the last two decades while government has failed to maximise revenue through excise taxes, according to a new study published on Thursday.

The real price of cigarettes has fallen by 21 percent in the past 24 years and the proportion of the retail price made up by taxes has dropped even further, according to a University of Cape Town (UCT) study backed by the Medical Research Council.
"In effect, the profit margin for the industry has been rising over the period, while at the same time excise tax revenues have declined," said Professor Iraj Abedian of UCT's School of Economics.
In 1990 prices, the real price of a packet of 20 cigarettes in 1971 was about 2.58 rand. In 1995 this had declined to 2.03 rand, after hitting a low of 1.48 rand in 1991.
In 1971, 45 percent of the retail price of cigarettes comprised excise duties, but by 1995 the figure had fallen to 20 percent.

"If government had attempted to maximise its revenue from cigarettes, excise receipts could have been up to 129 percent higher in 1991. In other words, government could have earned 3.33 bilion rand as opposed to an estimated 1.50 billion in revenue from cigarette tax," Abedian said.
The lost revenue translated into a 1.2 percent increase in total government revenue, or 8.4 percent of the health budget, he said.

South Africa's tobacco industy is locked in a fierce battle with Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma who warned last week she would outlaw all tobacco advertising if companies continued to bend the law on health warnings.

Market leader Rembrandt Group , with a market share of over 80 percent, fired back with a full-page open letter in a Sunday newspaper saying smuggling and customs corruption letting tonnes of contraband brands into the country were the real issues.
